title: Polynomial Separation between One-Way and Two-Way LOCC in Discrimination of Maximally Entangled States
summary: One-way local operations and classical communication (LOCC) can fail to distinguish four orthogonal maximally entangled states in every local dimension $d\ge4$. We show that every set of $k$ pairwise orthogonal maximally entangled states in $\mathbb C^d\otimes\mathbb C^d$ is perfectly distinguishable by an $A\to B\to A$ protocol whenever $d\ge Ck^4[\log(2k)]^ν$, for universal constants $C,ν>0$. A single feedback message therefore raises the number of candidates that can always be distinguished from a constant to $Ω\!\left(d^{1/4}/(\log d)^{ν/4}\right)$, establishing a polynomial separation…
